books.section: Topic 4.10 The Second Great Awakening, A. Religious and Spiritual Movements in Antebellum America

primary_sources: Charles G. Finney, "What a Revival of Religion Is" (Lectures on Revivals of Religion), 1835

stimulus.text: "When the churches are thus awakened and reformed, the reformation and salvation of sinners will follow.... Their hearts will be broken down and changed. Very often the most abandoned profligates are among the subjects. Harlots, and drunkards, and infidels, and all sorts of abandoned characters, are awakened and converted." — Charles G. Finney, "What a Revival of Religion Is," 1835
stimulus.source_note: Verbatim public-domain quotation from Charles G. Finney, Lectures on Revivals of Religion (1835), Lecture 1. Wording checked against the staged survivor barrons-2027-ch06-07 and the standard published text of the lecture.

source: original; stimulus is a verbatim public-domain quotation from Finney, Lectures on Revivals of Religion (1835)
stem: According to Finney, a revival of religion comes about primarily through which of the following?

options.text: God's sovereign choice to awaken only the elect
options.misconception: Finney's whole point was the opposite: sinners choose conversion, so revivals do not wait on election.

options.text: The preaching and prayer of awakened churches

options.misconception: Disestablishment is about church and state, not about what makes a revival happen.

options.text: The immigration of Catholics to American cities
options.misconception: Immigration is a different story — the passage is about churches waking sinners, not about who arrived in the cities.

rationales.A: Finney rejected predestination. His revivals did not wait on God's prior choice of the elect; they depended on human effort.
rationales.B: Finney says the churches must first be 'awakened and reformed,' and then 'the reformation and salvation of sinners will follow.' Preaching and prayer are the means that bring a revival.
rationales.C: Disestablishment changed the churches' legal standing, but Finney's revivals came from preaching, not from laws about establishment.
rationales.D: Catholic immigration grew in the 1840s, but it has nothing to do with how Finney said revivals happen.
rationales.general:
1. Read what comes first. Finney says 'when the churches are thus awakened and reformed, the reformation and salvation of sinners will follow.'
2. Name the means. Awakened churches preach and pray, and the worst sinners are converted.
3. Rule out the rest. Nothing here is about God choosing the elect, disestablishment, or immigration.
Background: Finney taught that a revival is not a miracle but the result of the right use of means — human effort under God.
Remember: in Finney's revivals, the churches act first and the sinners follow.
